assumptions: What SLATE doesn’t have for the retroactive months, recorded exactly: Connecticut asks about medical bills in the three months on the application (its W-1E); SLATE takes them as asked wherever care was had. A month’s eligibility is read as its own income on the earnings record and her status at the month’s end; HUSKY D has no asset test, and household isn’t kept. SLATE keeps one stretch of cover, so a retroactive month beyond a month she wasn’t eligible in isn’t covered, where Connecticut would cover it alone. A refund of what she paid goes to her bank, as repriceCare refunds; how a Connecticut provider refunds a patient once Medicaid pays isn’t read. Care Yale Health paid for isn’t reached back to.
SLATE keeps no HUSKY group but HUSKY D’s expansion adults, so § 71112’s two months for any other individual is read by no life.

The work rules aren’t read again for a retroactive month: from 2027 the one month reached is the month before the application, whose work rules the application reads (lookBack); an engagement check written there first was taken out, the whole suite passing without it.
New York’s Medicaid, Medi-Cal and Covered Connecticut keep the first of next month: their own rules on the beginning date weren’t read.
The renewal counts twelve (2026) or six (2027) months from the month of application, not from a retroactive month.
